table_title: List the major government space agencies enumerated in the Wikipedia 'List of government space agencies' Table[4] launch-related capabilities subset (24 agencies with at least an entry in the launch-capabilities table), with the full agency name, sponsoring country or intergovernmental organization, and founding year of the current named entity.
db_analog: SELECT agency, full_name, country_or_organization, founded FROM government_space_agencies WHERE agency_in_launch_related_capabilities_table = TRUE ORDER BY agency
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'List of government space agencies' master article, accessed 2026-05-14. Universe is the 24 government space agencies enumerated in the master article's Table[4] (per pandas.read_html — the launch-related capabilities subset table within the master article, with columns for Operates launch site / Suborbital launch capable / Orbital launch capable / Cryogenic rocket engine use / Reusable systems use). Table[4] membership is the source-defined 'major space agencies' subset — Table[4] membership alone defines the universe; the 5 launch-capability columns in Table[4] are not staged answer columns (the staged schema is Agency + Full Name + Country + Founded). Note: pandas.read_html parses some of Table[4]'s capability cells as NaN because the source renders Yes/No markers via flag/check icons rather than literal text strings; the source's visible Yes/No markers are not used to filter the universe in either direction. Per-row cells: Agency is the identifier verbatim from Table[4]'s Agency column (with footnote refs like '[2]', '[100]' stripped) — for most rows this is the acronym (NASA, ESA, JAXA, etc.); for two rows where the acronym 'ISA' would collide between Iranian Space Agency and Israel Space Agency, Table[4] uses the full name as the Agency identifier and the staged Agency value preserves this. Full Name is the full English name of the agency taken verbatim from the master Table[3] Name column. Country or Organization is the sovereign-state or intergovernmental sponsor taken verbatim from the master Table[3] Country column (with one normalization: the ESA row's Country cell in Table[3] is a comma-separated list of 22 European member states; the staged value normalizes this to the descriptive label 'European Space Agency member states'). Founded is the 4-digit integer year extracted from Table[3]'s Founded column, using the year corresponding to the CURRENT named entity in multi-year founding-history cells (e.g., 'CONAE' = 1991 in '1961 (CNIE) 28 May 1991 (CONAE)'; 'POLSA' = 2014 in '29 Sep 1976 (CBK PAN) 26 Sep 2014 (POLSA)'; 'NATA' = 2023 in '1980s (KCST) 2013 (NADA) 2023 (NATA)'; 'Soviet space program' = 1955 founding year per '1955 disbanded 25 Dec 1991'). The 24-row universe is stable on a multi-year horizon: new space agencies may be founded and Wikipedia may eventually add new rows to Table[4]; current agencies are unlikely to be retired (the defunct Soviet space program † is staged with its † marker per the source).
_extraction_notes: Original instance chipping `factual_lookup` from gap 1 to **gap 0** (SATURATING the category at 5/5 — FIFTH CATEGORY TO FULLY CLEAR after multi_attribute_projection 8/8, set_operation 8/8, set_filter 5/5, causal 5/5; 4 staged of 5 before this staging: eu_member_states_accession_years, chemical_elements_discovered_1869_1945, twelve_olympians_greek_to_roman, oceanic_trenches_named_deeps; this instance brings the count to 5/5). User-selected after the picker-recommended factual_lookup saturator candidates list (world's tallest dams — taken by parallel agent; major space agencies — this instance; major straits of the world). Domain Science/Space Exploration extends the existing Space Exploration subdomain from 3 event-keyed instances (crewed_spaceflight_fatal_incidents, apollo_lunar_landing_mission_crews, notable_robotic_spacecraft_missions) to 4 instances with the FIRST organization-keyed Space-Exploration entity. Entity class organizations/space-agencies is a NEW fine-class within the under-represented organizations bucket (bucket count 2 → 3, joining universities and companies). Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, source_count = 1 — the master 'List of government space agencies' article supplies all 4 cells per row via its Table[3] master + Table[4] launch-capable subset (both tables in the same source URL). Pipeline: (1) fetch the cited master Wikipedia article HTML, (2) parse Table[4] (24-row launch-related capabilities subset) to identify the universe membership by Agency-column value, (3) cross-reference each Table[4] agency against Table[3] (89-row master) by acronym/name match to extract the Country and Name and Founded cells, (4) for each row, stage Agency from Table[4]'s Agency column (footnote refs stripped; full name preserved for Iran/Israel rows to avoid PK collision), Full Name from Table[3]'s Name column verbatim, Country or Organization from Table[3]'s Country column with ESA member-state normalization, Founded as 4-digit integer year of the current named entity from Table[3]'s Founded column. Result: 24 rows × 4 columns, PK on Agency, 0 duplicates. Country distribution: 24 distinct sovereign-state or intergovernmental sponsors (Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, ESA member states, France, India, Iran, Israel, Italy, Japan, South Korea, Mexico, USA, North Korea, New Zealand, Poland, Russia, Sweden, Ukraine, Pakistan, Soviet Union †, UK). Founded year distribution (sum = 24): 1950s 2 (NASA 1958, Soviet space program 1955), 1960s 3 (CNES 1961, ISRO 1969, SUPARCO 1961), 1970s 2 (ESA 1975, SNSA 1972), 1980s 4 (Israel Space Agency 1983, ASI 1988, CSA 1989, KARI 1989), 1990s 5 (CONAE 1991, Roscosmos 1992, SSAU 1992, CNSA 1993, AEB 1994), 2000s 2 (JAXA 2003, Iranian Space Agency 2004), 2010s 5 (MSA 2010, UKSA 2010, POLSA 2014, NZSA 2016, ASA 2018), 2020s 1 (NATA 2023). Confidence gradient: very-LLM-knowable cells include the canonical major agencies (NASA, ESA, JAXA, ISRO, CNSA, Roscosmos — all well-documented and globally-recognized); mid-difficulty cells include the well-known but less-headline-grabbing agencies (CNES France 1961, ASI Italy 1988, CSA Canada 1989, KARI South Korea 1989); harder calibration cells include the more obscure or recently-founded agencies (CONAE Argentina 1991, AEB Brazil 1994, SUPARCO Pakistan 1961, SSAU Ukraine 1992, NATA North Korea 2023, MSA Mexico 2010). The Founded cell tests recall of agency founding years from compound multi-year founding histories (e.g., CONAE founded in 1991 succeeding CNIE 1961). Notable design choices: (a) Iran and Israel use full-name Agency values per Table[4]'s disambiguation convention (both agencies share the acronym 'ISA'); (b) ESA row uses 'European Space Agency member states' as Country to handle the 22-member-state concatenation in the source; (c) Soviet space program is staged with the † defunct-marker per source; (d) All 24 Table[4] members are retained per source-defined membership rather than filtered out by any capability-based rule; the staged schema does not include the launch-capability columns, so their values are not staged answer cells. (Note: pandas.read_html parses some of Table[4]'s capability cells as NaN because the source uses flag/check icons rather than text — the source visibly shows Yes/No markers for CSA, MSA, POLSA, UKSA, etc.; the universe-membership rule does not depend on these markers.)
